item.title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 1: Wide receiver shuffling amidst injuries
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens were victorious in the season opener yesterday, defeating the Indianapolis Colts in a 41-23 win. Here is a breakdown of the team’s player snap counts on offense and defense. Offense Jackson and the starting offensive line played all 68 snaps. Backup offensive tackle Carson Vinson saw seven snaps as an extra blocker […]
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravens were victorious in the season opener yesterday, defeating the Indianapolis Colts in a 41-23 win. Here is a breakdown of the team’s player snap counts on offense and defense.

Offense

  • QB: Lamar Jackson 68
  • RB: Derrick Henry 37, Justice Hill 31
  • WR: Rashod Bateman 53, Ja’Kobi Lane 27, Chris Moore 20, LaJohntay Wester 20, Zay Flowers 20
  • TE: Mark Andrews 49, Durham Smythe 42, Matthew Hibner 23, Josh Cuevas 6
  • OL: Ronnie Stanley 68, John Simpson 68, Jovaughn Gwyn 68, Vega Ioane 68, Roger Rosengarten 68, Carson Vinson 7

Jackson and the starting offensive line played all 68 snaps. Backup offensive tackle Carson Vinson saw seven snaps as an extra blocker in jumbo formations. In the backfield, Derrick Henry played just over half of the team’s offensive snaps and rushed for 144 yards with three touchdowns on 20 attempts. Justice Hill played 31 snaps and received seven touches in total.

The snap counts at wide receiver are the biggest notable story. With Devontez Walker inactive due to an ankle injury, the Ravens suffered two more injuries at the position. Zay Flowers played 20 snaps in the first half before exiting with a hamstring injury, totaling 150 yards and a touchdown on five catches. Likewise, Ja’Kobi Lane was sidelined for the rest of the game after he too left early with a wrist ailment following 27 snaps. Lane’s first NFL touchdown catch was called back due to a penalty.

With both players sidelined, Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester took on elevated roles, each playing 20 offensive snaps. Moore had a long 53-yard catch and Wester caught two passes, in addition to both players’ duties as primary returners on special teams. Rashod Bateman started the game and played all but one snap, however he was targeted only once with no catches.

Mark Andrews unsurprisingly led the tight end room with 49 snaps, catching four passes on six targets. Veteran Durham Smythe played 42 snaps as a primary blocker. Matthew Hibner is clearly third in the pecking order ahead of Josh Cuevas, out-snapping his fellow rookie 23 to six. Hibner caught one pass for 13 yards.

Defense

  • DL: Travis Jones 31, Calais Campbell 29, Broderick Washington 21, John Jenkins 13, Aeneas Peebles 10
  • EDGE: Tavius Robinson 44, Trey Hendrickson 40, Mike Green 17, Zion Young 12
  • ILB: Roquan Smith 54, Trenton Simpson 32
  • CB: Nate Wiggins 54, Marlon Humphrey 48, Keyon Martin 23, Chidobe Awuzie 6
  • S: Kyle Hamilton 54, Malaki Starks 54, Jaylinn Hawkins 52

All five of the Ravens’ defensive lineman saw 10+ snaps in this game as Nnami Madubuike’s return to action awaits. Travis Jones led the way with 31 snaps, closely followed by fellow veterans Calais Campbell (29) and Broderick Washington (21). John Jenkins and Aeneas Peebles combined to play 23 snaps.

Tavius Robinson (44) and Trey Hendrickson (40) had a commanding snap share on the edge. Robinson had four quarterback hits and a sack, while Hendrickson was charted for eight pressures. Mike Green only played 17 snaps as the third banana, while rookie Zion Young’s debut saw him on the field for 12 defensive plays. Roquan Smith played every defensive snap and had a starring performance with an interception and team-high 11 tackles. Next to him, Trenton Simpson played 32 snaps and drew the start in the absence of Teddye Buchanan once again.

Nate Wiggins did not leave the field and had a pass breakup in his 54 snaps. Marlon Humphrey’s 48 snaps were productive, as the veteran forced a fumble and had a key pass knockdown on a deep attempt in single coverage. Nickel corner Keyon Martin’s 23 snaps were third-most at the position. Surprisingly, Chidobe Awuzie only played six defensive snaps. T.J. Tampa suffered a knee injury and did not return to the game.

The Ravens’ trio of safeties were on the field together for all but two plays where Jaylinn Hawkins was relieved. Hamilton and Starks each played 54 snaps. Hawkins occupying a near every-down role likely explains the lack of significant snaps for Martin and Awuzie at cornerback.

item.title: Game Recap: Saints visit Lions in season opener
item.description: Catch up on all the action from the Saints in Detroit on Sunday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints were looking to pull off a road upset against the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. Here’s a recap of all the action.

First Quarter

The hosts got the ball to begin the game and went three-and-out. But the Saints didn’t fare much better on their opening series, with a 9-yard pass from Tyler Shough to Devaughn Vele marking the only first-down gain of the drive.

Jared Goff and the Lions offense proceeded to get going on their second possession. A 19-yard connection with Sam LaPorta preceded a pair of big bursting runs from Jahmyr Gibbs to put Detroit in the red zone.

From there, the Lions capitalised, with a 1-yard score from Gibbs capping off an 89-yard touchdown drive.

Second Quarter

The teams then exchanged a number of punts as the game moved into the second quarter. Shough did find Chris Olave on a few big throws, though the Saints never moved into scoring position.

Detroit would then turn it over through a Gibbs fumble after a successful Saints challenge, but the visitors returned the favor when Shough threw an interception a few plays later.

The Lions went three-and-out again, pinning New Orleans deep in their own half. Shough was able to move the drive past midfield with a 19-yard throw to Bryce Lance, but a sack a few plays later from Aidan Hutchinson forced a Saints punt just before the half.

Third Quarter

Trailing 7-0, Shough threw another interception on the first play of the second half.

Detroit took advantage of the short field as Gibbs continued to punish the Saints defense, breaking off for an 18-yard run before eventually running in another 1-yard score to push the lead to 14-0.

Shough proceeded to fumble early on the ensuing possession to give the Lions yet another short field. Goff connected with Amon-Ra St Brown for a 19-yard touchdown pass to give Detroit a 21-0 advantage.

Then, at last, the Saints offense burst into life. A 47-yard pass to Olave and a 9-yard throw to Noah Fant put the black and gold on the edge of the red zone.

A few plays later, including a third-down scramble from Shough for a first down, Kendre Miller ran in an 8-yard touchdown to get the visitors on the board.

The Saints defense responded with a perfect series of their own, forcing a three-and-out.

Shough picked up where he left off, completing his first three throws of the ensuing drive for 31 yards. A defensive pass interference call put the Saints down at the 1-yard line, before Shough found Vele for his first touchdown pass of the season to cut into the lead again.

Fourth Quarter

Now leading just 21-14, Goff and the Lions were forced into another quick punt.

The Saints offense continued their momentum, as Travis Etienne ran for 14 yards to begin another scoring series. Shough’s 31-yard connection with Vele put the visitors in the red zone, though this time they were held to a field goal attempt.

Daniel Carlson’s 28-yard chip shot put the score at 21-17.

Having nearly blown their lead entirely, the Lions at last found some life. A facemask penalty against Tyree Wilson meant they began their drive at midfield.

Gibbs continued to have success running the football, but the Saints defense did manage to hold Detroit to a field goal. Jake Bates’ 23-yard kick put the lead back to seven, at 24-17.

Needing a touchdown to tie the game, the Saints quickly found themselves on 4th-and-12 with the game on the line. Shough delivered, finding Lance for 15 yards.

He connected with Vele on the next play for another first down, and then connected with Olave on another bomb for a 42-yard gain. Juwan Johnson caught the 9-yard touchdown pass a play later, and the extra point tied the game at 24-24.

With just over a minute remaining, Detroit would go three-and-out, giving New Orleans a slim chance at winning the game in regulation after an Etienne run and an 18-yard catch from Johnson gave Shough time to spike the ball for a long field goal.

But Carlson’s 62-yard effort went wide right as the clock expired.

Overtime

The Saints deferred to Detroit, who put together a 70-yard touchdown drive highlighted by a 22-yard pass from Goff to Jameson Williams to set up 1st-and-goal. St Brown caught the touchdown pass to put the Lions up 31-24.

Needing a touchdown of their own, Shough threw for 20 yards to Olave on another fourth-down conversion as the Saints moved past midfield. He found Fant for 10 yards amidst short runs from Miller and Etienne, before finding Johnson for 27 yards to set up 1st-and-goal.

It was Fant again who caught the 8-yard touchdown pass to put New Orleans down by just a point.

Kellen Moore elected to go for two and the win, as opposed to tying the game and giving Detroit a chance to score again.

But the Lions defense prevailed, as Shough’s pass intended for Lance had almost no chance. Despite a resilient comeback effort from the black and gold, the Lions emerged victorious, 31-30.

If it’s any consolation, all three NFC South rivals dropped their opening game on Sunday. Next up for the Saints is a visit to the Baltimore Ravens on September 20.

item.title: NFL Week 2 odds: Seahawks open as heavy favorites vs. Cardinals
item.description: Seattle is a 5.5-point road favorite against Arizona, with Drew Lock expected to start at quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks are comfortable favorites against their division rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 2.

After opening the 2026 season with a 13-10 comeback victory over the New England Patriots, the Seahawks will hit the road for their first away game of the season when they visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 20.

According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook, Seattle is a 5.5-point favorite (-110). The Seahawks’ moneyline is -235, while Arizona sits at +194. The game total is currently set at 41.5 points.

That makes Seattle a relatively significant road favorite, but the betting line comes with an important wrinkle: Drew Lock is expected to start at quarterback against Arizona with Sam Darnold sidelined by his injury.

Darnold suffered the glute injury on Seattle’s opening drive against New England and did not return. Lock took over and ultimately helped the Seahawks complete the comeback, finishing the game 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown.

The latest reports indicate that Darnold is expected to miss the Cardinals game, putting Lock in line for his first start of the 2026 season. That makes the -5.5 spread particularly interesting. Seattle is being asked to cover more than a field goal on the road despite making a quarterback change just one game into the season.

Arizona won’t be an easy opponent, either. The Cardinals opened their season with a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, giving them a victory on the road before returning home to Seattle.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, are coming off a defensive performance in which they intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to help overturn their only 10-0 deficit and get the opening night victory.

That combination helps explain why the total is relatively low at 41.5 points. FanDuel’s current market projects a game in which Seattle is favored to win, but not necessarily one expected to turn into a shootout.

And, honestly, what else should we expect from a game in Glendale? There’s nothing particularly normal about playing the Cardinals in the desert, where these matchups have a habit of turning chaotic and unpredictable. Seattle should be prepared for another one of those games.

item.title: The Takeaway: Not much new to see in the Eagles’ escape over the Commanders
item.description: The Eagles’ 2025 opener felt a lot like what we saw in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
By the time Lincoln Financial Field’s clock struck 0:00 late Sunday afternoon and the Eagles had survived a 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, a palpable sense of relief could be felt by the fanbase.

For the sixth straight time under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles won their opening game. It is the longest active streak in the NFL and it is always better to start 1-0 than 0-1.

Just ask the Dallas Cowboys.

While the Eagles’ defense looked absolutely gassed by the end of it, they managed one last goal-line, two-point conversion stand, and spent the better part of the first three quarters limiting Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense for most of the afternoon.

It was reminiscent of a season ago, when the defense carried an offense that had trouble maintaining consistency.

Week 1 was our first opportunity to see what the new scheme was going to look like under Sean Mannion and how the passing game would function without A.J. Brown. It was also our first look at an offensive line that featured an injured-and-struggling Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson. We finally got to see if Hurts would spend more time under center, how that would affect the passing game and whether Saquon Barkley would be more productive in the new offense than he was a year ago.

At the end of the day, the offense looked a whole lot like it did a season ago.

And it was Jalen Hurts who saved them.

There were entire quarters where the offense did nothing but go 3-and-out, but they also committed no turnovers. The short intermediate passing game over the middle was largely non existent, but there were several explosive plays and two TDs to Dallas Goedert up the seam. Saquon Barkley largely struggled again behind and offensive line that is nowhere near what it was in 2024, but broke off a long run and put up decent numbers otherwise.

Baby steps, perhaps?

Jalen Hurts, of course, remained the same, both in good ways and in bad.

Hurts made the play of the game with his legs in the 4th quarter, converting a 3rd-and-18 with a 22-yard gain to help dig the Birds out of their offensive malaise.

It was vintage playmaking by the still-fleet veteran, weaving his way through the defense to convert a first down when nothing was schemed open and his offensive line was leaking oil. And as in years past, it was Hurts’ deep balls and ability to play out of structure that generated most of the offensive output.

There’s good news and bad news in that.

The bad news is the Sean Mannion offense was supposed to create opportunities in the run and pass game for players. It’s only Week 1, and Mannion’s scheme deserves much more time to find its sea legs, but watching Dickerson and Jurgens struggle in both facets of the game was disheartening, to say the least. The run game looked a lot like it did last season and, as Tom Brady noted on the Fox telecast, there were times Hurts dropped his eyes and watched the pass rush when his first read was taken away.

This is all going to take time. Patience is required, and hopefully it will all work out. In the meantime, Hurts spent much of Sunday improvising and relying on his previous strenghts — his legs and the bomb.

The deep ball to DeVonta Smith along the sideline in the 3rd quarter was gorgeous, as was the toe-dragging catch by his new No. 1 receiver.

And his 64-yard deep bomb to Dontayvion Wicks in the 1st quarter was a thing of beauty.

Like a season ago, the Eagles showed less play-to-play consistency, but more big splashes. It’s two different ways to score points and, on Sunday, it was enough against a Commanders team that, barring a few boneheaded mistakes, probably should have won.

Defensively, Vic Fangio’s unit dominated for three quarters before the heat, humidity, and Daniels’ legs, wore them down. Zach Baun was incredible on Sunday, and the defensive line got persistent pressure on Daniels, if not sacks or turnovers. They made life uncomfortable for just about everyone. It was not Cooper DeJean’s best day, nor was it Jihaad Campbell’s. The safeties left gaps in the middle of the field. But it was enough.

The big takeaway after Sunday’s 24-22 win was that it felt a whole lot like games the Eagles won last year. Never comfortable, ugly at times, finding a way to survive, overly reliant on Hurts to figure it out on his own.

Happily, he did on Sunday.

In Week 1, you take the win no matter how you get it, and hope things look a bit better as the schedule rolls along.

item.title: Rams had amazing offseason, dud Week 1
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams had a rough Week 1, and plenty more news on a Monday!
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams had one of the best on paper off-season’s in modern sports, then followed that up with a horrible Week 1. Things can always be worse, but the Week 1 that L.A. just has proven again why picking a Super Bowl winner in August is nearly an impossible task.

Starting with the offseason, some would say the Rams received too much coverage the last few months, and that’s fair, but the Rams received so much coverage because they were constantly generating news.

Trading for Trent Mcduffie, adding Jaylen Watson, trying to figure out their special teams, trading for Myles Garrett, keeping the offense in tact including Matthew Stafford, and Aaron Donald’s future with the team dominated NFL talk for months leading up to the 2026 season.

Then, Week 1 actually happened.

The Super Bowl favorite Rams got slapped in the face by the San Francisco 49ers. The Seattle Seahawks showed they can win with a backup quarterback and can still ride their defense. The Arizona Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Chargers in a major early season upset.

Now, the Rams are looking up in the NFC West, and as of one week into the season, they look a bit lost. Myles Garrett is going to IR. AD must be wondering what he is coming back to? Sean McVay needs to figure it out.

It’s been an interesting Week 1 for the Rams. They have more than a few games left. We’ll see what happens.

A Whole Lot Changed In One Week For The Rams (defector)

“How best to react to the latest news on the Los Angeles Rams? Easy: with complete abandon and logical recklessness. That’s how the veterans do it.

Said latest news: that massive offseason acquisition Myles Garrett has fouled his knee, failed to will it healthy again, and now will have surgery that will take out all of September and a chunk of October as well. Garrett was the big swing of the summer, but the fact that it was the Rams that took it is no surprise. General manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay love acquisitional bat speed more than nearly any team not named Real Madrid or Barcelona, and between Garrett and veteran ace in the hole Aaron Donald, they surely constructed the most unsettling defensive front since their own Fearsome Foursome six decades ago.“

Myles Garrett Goes On IR After Knee Surgery: What Does It Mean For Rams? (foxsports)

“Star edge rusher Myles Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his knee and will be placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least four games, The Ringer first reported. FOX Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer later confirmed the news.

“Myles Garrett didn’t do a lot of practice in this training camp,” Glazer said on “FOX NFL Kickoff.” “He had a knee injury. You saw him there the other night against [San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle] Trent Williams; he just wasn’t right. So the team decided they’re going to have him undergo arthroscopic knee surgery.”

Maxx Crosby reportedly turned down Rams interest after Ravens trade collapsed (sports.yah00)

“League interest remained significant. Reports indicate that multiple teams contacted the Raiders after the Ravens trade collapsed. The Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49erswere among clubs reported to have monitored the situation. Despite that interest, no offer matched what Las Vegas believed Crosby was worth, making a second trade unlikely.

With Crosby remaining off the market, the Rams eventually shifted their attention elsewhere and later completed their blockbuster acquisition of Garrett. The move helped reshape Los Angeles’ defense, but the latest report suggests the organization may have initially preferred a different path.“

3 things Rams can learn from Giants’ win ahead of Week 2 matchup (ramswire)

“With the Rams looking to avoid a 0-2 start, here are three major lessons they must learn this week after New York dazzled in head coach John Harbaugh’s debut.

Isaiah Likely will be a matchup problem

Giants tight end Isaiah Likely impressed during his first few seasons with the Baltimore Ravens, even proving he was more productive than incumbent starter Mark Andrews when given an extended run of play. That chance never materialized, but in his debut with New York, he was ungardable.

Rams gave Aaron Donald’s contract incentives creative nicknames (sports.yahoo)

“The Los Angeles Rams do things their way, and one of the most defining elements of the team’s independent ideas is how they go about their roster. Their beliefs behind roster construction are often subjected to media attention, as the franchise leverages its top draft picks for star players, using its scouting and developmental departments to fill out the roster.

However, that’s not the only aspect of their construction that is unique to Los Angeles. ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams give nicknames to incentive packages in their contracts, with Aaron Donald having monikers that define his return perfectly.

He has one incentive named “I’m Back” and another called “I Got 99 Problems.”

Rams’ Sean McVay reveals wife’s reality check after mulling media jump following losing season in 2022 (foxnews)

“The Rams were 5-12 in 2022 – one year after beating the Cincinnati Bengals to win Super Bowl LVI. He said in an interview on “60 Minutes,” which aired Sunday night, that he was in a “dark” place and had to come to grips with the fact that a few losses weren’t a reflection on himself.

He said his wife, Veronika Khomyn, hit him with a reality check.

“I was ready to run away from coaching and hide behind a convenient narrative of some media opportunities,” he explained. “I’ll never forget, I was explaining to my wife, Veronika, it was a daunting task ahead for the ’23 season and I remember telling her, ‘Maybe I’ll take a year off,’ and she said, ‘That never sounded like the kind of leader you wanted to be.’”

Rams coach Sean McVay “tormented,” even with the team as Super Bowl favorite (cbssports)

“”You’re either in a storm, you’re coming out of one or you’re getting ready to go back into it,” McVay said. “And it’s one of those three things. But how you handle that is the separator.”

How McVay’s handled winning and losing 

McVay’s Super Bowl win came after acquiring quarterback Matthew Stafford . But the coach’s joy over the win was fleeting.

“The lies I told myself were, ‘I won’t be happy until I — until we win one.’ Or, ‘I win one,'” McVay said. “It was a lot more selfish. And, you know, you’re embarrassed to kind of look back on how you got to where you did.”

The Rams’ 2022 Super Bowl win was followed by a losing season. 

“It revealed a lot of insecurities that I had. My identity was so tied up in winning and losing games, and that was where I felt like my self-worth lied,” McVay said. “It was very revealing of how fragile I was and all the insecurities that I did have.”

NFL Week 1 winners, losers: Deshaun Watson disastrous in Browns offense, Bears light up scoreboard (cbssports)

“While the small sample size of one game can cloud reality, there are some cases where Week 1 tells the football world all it needs to know about a particular team or individual player. In Watson’s case, a poor season debut might be all it takes to write the book on his run as the Browns’ starting quarterback. For the Bears, a 59-point onslaught is compelling evidence that they are in for a monster year.

In an 18-week season, there is still ample time to right wrongs and for strengths to devolve into weaknesses. But for now, some are off to hot starts while others could not have opened the year in a worse fashion.

Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday’s Week 1 action.“

2026 NFL season, Week 1: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com)

“Bears offense enters a new orbit. After jumping from the bottom of the league to sixth overall in total yards last season, Chicago’s offense used Week 1 to send the clearest message that it has an extra gear to hit in Year 2 of the Ben Johnson era. The Bears dropped 59 points on Carolina — their most in a game since the 1980 season — with a balanced and unrelenting attack. Caleb Williams looked masterful for much of the game, making highlight-reel plays with his arm and legs. He’s the first player in franchise history to post 200-plus passing yards, two or more passing touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and two or more rushing scores in a single game, per NFL Research. Running backs D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai each reached the century mark in rushing yards. On a day when the defense gave up 37 points, Chicago won by 22 points. For so many years, that kind of outcome was something Bears fans could only dream about.“

Notable injuries, news from Sunday’s Week 1 games: Ravens’ Zay Flowers exits with hamstring injury (nfl.com)

“Here are the injuries and news we’re monitoring around the league on this Week 1 Sunday:“

Rams open as big favorites vs. Giants in Week 2 (ramswire)

“These two teams will now square off in another prime-time matchup next Monday night at SoFi Stadium. The Rams will be well-rested after returning from Melbourne, while the Giants will have to fly across the country for a marquee matchup against the Super Bowl favorites.

Despite their differing records, it’s the Rams who are heavy favorites over the Giants. Here are the opening odds from BetMGM.“

I’m concerned about the defense. They were getting abused in the run game and Shula did not adjust. Kept running the four man fronts. I don’t recall any run blitzes or taking a safety off to add another DT.
